notes.decision: Translated 'they dwell/are situated' tentatively. The form is irregular Lycopolitan; likely related to ϩⲱⲡ 'be hidden' or to a stative of ϣⲱⲡⲉ 'become, be.' The contrast inside/outside in lines 2-4 indicates the verb predicates location of envy and falsehood.

Rendered 'joints' tentatively. The lexeme is unattested in glossary or standard dictionaries. Position in the inventory (stones, bones, joints) supports a hard structural body-element. Possibly related to ⲗⲁⲕ/ⲗⲁϫ 'fragment' or to a Greek-derived term for ligaments/sinews.

Rendered 'likewise/touch' tentatively. May represent Lyc. ϩⲱⲱϥ 'also' or a verb of contact. The construction 'outside however, X in the witnessings of lies' demands either an adverbial connector or a verb of dwelling/touching parallel to ϩⲩⲱⲟⲉ in line 2.
Rendered 'with wrath.' ⲩⲛⲉⲩⲧ likely Lyc. for ⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩⲧ/ⲱⲛⲧ̄ 'wrath, anger.' Fits the active hostility against the teacher.

Rendered 'they place their trust.' Probable Lyc. reduction of ϣⲁⲩ-(ⲟⲩ)ⲁϩ-ⲛⲁⲍ(ⲧ)ϩ̄ 'they habitually place faith/trust' (cf. ⲡⲉϩⲛⲁⲍⲧⲉ 'his faith' in glossary). The construction ⲍⲟⲩⲟ ⲩⲁϩⲛⲁⲍϩ ⲁⲡⲁⲟⲉ 'exceedingly they place trust in falsehood' fits the apostate-vs-teacher polemic.

Rendered 'in falsehood.' ⲡⲁⲟⲉ here likely a Lyc. doublet of ⲡⲟⲁⲗ 'lie/falsehood' (line 5). Cf. accumulated vocab entry tentatively glossing 'distance/far reach,' which does not fit this immediate context.
Translated 'who are diminished in power.' ⲥⲁⲃⲕ qualitative 'become small'; ⲧⲟⲁⲙ Lyc. for ϫⲟⲙ 'power.' Refers to the apostates whose spiritual capacity has shrunk.

notes.coptic_form: ⲡⲉⲧⲥⲛⲟⲩⲭⲉ ⲙ̄ⲙⲁϩ ⲁⲧⲣⲉⲓ̈ⲧⲉ ⲧⲏⲣⲥ̄ ⲛⲧⲉ ⲡⲱⲛⲍ̄
notes.decision: Translated 'which casts him out from the entire kind of the Living One.' ⲣⲉⲓ̈ⲧⲉ Lyc. for 'kind, form' (in glossary); ⲡⲱⲛⲍ̄ 'the Living One' (the cosmic Life-principle, possibly Mother of Life). The wickedness of Matter excludes the apostate from the family of Light.

Translated 'doubt ... contend.' ⲟⲱⲧⲧ likely = Coptic ⲱⲧⲧ̄ 'doubt, waver.' ⲁⲧⲣⲓ̈ⲉ uncertain — possibly a verb of contention/disputation paired with doubt. Both are negated conjunctives describing what the wise man avoids.

Rendered 'He who shall come forth.' The verb ⲟⲁⲗⲧ is unidentified — possibly Lyc. for ⲱⲗⲧ̄ (rest, depart) or ⲟⲩⲱⲗ (go), or a future relative of an unattested motion-verb. The construction ⲉⲓ ⲍⲓⲧⲉϩⲉⲍⲏ 'comes before him' indicates a serial-verb of arriving in the presence of the apostle/teacher. The line closes the kephalaion as a sapiential statement about the faithful one who will appear before the Lord.
Decorative chapter-heading ornament, possibly a Coptic numeral (74?) framing the new chapter title. Not translated; rendered as ⊙. Three occurrences in lines 27, 29 frame the title.

notes.decision: Chapter heading: 'Concerning the Living Fire, that it exists in eight places.' ⲧⲥⲉⲧⲉ ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ̄ is the standard Manichaean technical term for the Living Fire — one of the Five Living Elements. The chapter enumerates eight cosmological loci where this fire is present, beginning with the Land of Light.
Translated 'the first place.' ⲧⲧⲩⲁⲣⲡ = ⲧϣⲟⲣⲡ̄ feminine 'the first' (Lyc. ⲩⲁⲣⲡ for ϣⲟⲣⲡ̄, cf. accumulated ⲡⲱⲁⲣⲡ ⲛⲣⲱⲙⲉ 'First Man'). ⲙⲙⲁ = 'place' (= ⲛ̄-ⲙⲁ).
